question: what are the warranties on electronics products

result.answer:
The provided evidence outlines a statutory guarantee under section 59 of the Australian Consumer Law, which applies when goods are supplied to a consumer in trade or commerce, excluding sales by auction. [1] This guarantee ensures that the manufacturer will comply with any express warranty given or made by the manufacturer regarding the goods. [1] Similarly, there is a guarantee that the supplier will comply with any express warranty given or made by the supplier in relation to the goods. [1]

The text does not specify the content of express warranties for electronics products or list particular warranty terms; it only establishes the legal guarantee that such warranties, if made, must be complied with by the manufacturer or supplier. [1]

evidence.title: Australian Consumer Law — s 59: Guarantee as to express warranties
evidence.text: 59 Guarantee as to express warranties 1 If: a a person supplies, in trade or commerce, goods to a consumer; and b the supply does not occur by way of sale by auction; there is a guarantee that the manufacturer of the goods will comply with any express warranty given or made by the manufacturer in relation to the goods. 2 If: a a person supplies, in trade or commerce, goods to a consumer; and b the supply does not occur by way of sale by auction; there is a guarantee that the supplier will comply with any express warranty given or made by the supplier in relation to the goods. Subdivision B—Guarantees relating to the supply of services
